clue.text: Opposing view in paper that's written about journal

parts.note: the Mirror is a British daily newspaper

indicators.note: one piece is written around another, so the letters for that's enclose the letters for journal

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a magazine, shortened to mag, is a periodical journal

explanation.surface: A contrary opinion appears in a newspaper's article on a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' is the British tabloid, not a sheet; 'in' is a link word, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflection reverses left and right, so it is the exact opposite or counterpart of the original view.

clue.text: Put up girl guide?

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up means reading it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to accommodate a young member of the Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart of an area serves to guide a traveller on their way.

clue.text: Letter from Greece containing current, or old money?

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it, so the Greek letter surrounds the other piece

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
in means fashionable or current

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a Greek letter contains electric current, or old coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' tempts as I, the physics symbol, but here it is IN, meaning fashionable; 'or' is a link. RHINO is dated British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old slang word for cash, used in Britain from the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Head's back in charge of firm, taking rise and position

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters rise, reading bottom to top, so both short pieces are turned backwards

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
to put something is to position it

explanation.surface: Someone at the rear of the company is in charge, getting a pay rise and a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking rise' turns ICCO round to OCCI; 'of' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The anatomical term names the rear part of the skull.

clue.text: Offhand, as one Tory maybe, with easy victory over unions

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a Conservative is an example of a Member of Parliament, MP
a romp is a win achieved with ease
TU stands for trade union

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician speaks casually after winning comfortably against the unions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word; a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without preparation is spontaneous, made up on the spot.

clue.text: Charts a sailor's looking up

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up means the word reads from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: Navigation charts belonging to a sailor are being consulted.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of maps is a collection of charts.

clue.text: Spell out East — times had by poet

parts.note: x is the multiplication sign, read as times
Ezra Pound was an American poet

explanation.surface: Someone describes the East and the times a poet lived through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something in detail is to set it out fully.

clue.text: Recall name of police dog

indicators.note: to recall here is to call back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the Northern Ireland police force

explanation.surface: Someone tries to remember what a police dog is called.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel or worthless hound is a contemptuous word for a dog.

clue.text: One far from constant or calm he recollected one harassed

indicators.note: collected again into a fresh order, so the letters are gathered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A harassed person, normally steady or serene, gathers his thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One far from constant' reads like a description of a person, which is the point: the lizard's name is used for a fickle person. 'or' and 'harassed' only colour the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The lizard famous for changing colour gives its name to a fickle person who keeps shifting.

clue.text: Kent area produced portrait painter and crime writer

parts.note: George Romney was an eighteenth-century English portrait painter
Ngaio Marsh was a New Zealand crime novelist

explanation.surface: A region of Kent gave the world a painter and a detective novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' is a link. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a flat wetland district in south-east Kent, England.

clue.text: British civil servant quoting a law?

indicators.note: quoting a word means saying it out loud, so a word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: a principle is a fundamental law

explanation.surface: A British official is heard reciting a statute.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British civil service a Principal is a middle-ranking grade of official.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a grade of officer in the British civil service.

clue.text: Afternoon when little girl's burst into that song?

indicators.note: one piece bursts into another, ending up inside it

parts.note: p.m. stands for post meridiem, the afternoon
Sal is a short form of the girl's name Sally

explanation.surface: A small girl starts singing a tune one afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' and 'that' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred hymn from the biblical book is a religious song.

clue.text: Arachnid's name omitted in a sign ()

indicators.note: something is left out, so a letter is dropped from the word for the creature

parts.note: a scorpion is an arachnid

explanation.surface: The name of a spider-like creature is missing from a notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; the printed clue lost its letter count to OCR.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Paid off spy I trained

indicators.note: off here means wrong or out of order, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: An agent says he was paid off after his training.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaried post receives a regular stipend, so it is a paid one.

clue.text: Provide jam and milk

definitions.meaning: to cram or crush things together is to create a crowded jam
to milk someone is to extort money from them

explanation.surface: Someone is told to offer preserves and dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' is a crush, not a preserve, and 'milk' means extort, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To press into a tight space makes a jam; to extract money from someone is to bleed them dry.

clue.text: Far from fit during a gym session

parts.note: in means during, as in in the morning
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Someone is out of shape in the middle of a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsuitable or inappropriate is far from fitting.

clue.text: Like chap coming into money, becoming superior

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: one piece comes into another, ending up inside it

parts.note: a cent is a coin, a unit of money
Dan is a man's name

explanation.surface: Something resembles a man inheriting a fortune and rising in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising to a position of dominance means gaining power over others.

clue.text: Impossible plan churchwarden finally committed to paper

parts.note: a churchwarden is a long clay tobacco pipe

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it sits beside

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper

explanation.surface: A church official's unrealistic scheme is finally written down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churchwarden' looks like a parish officer but is the long clay pipe; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful hope that will never come true is an unrealistic scheme.

clue.text: A thing for lighting fires?

parts.note: read 'a thing for' as an obsession with, so the phrase describes a compulsion to set things alight rather than a match

explanation.definitionFit: An irresistible urge to start blazes is an obsession, or mania, with burning.

clue.text: Old person auditing, say, one's funds

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an auditor is someone who checks the accounts, a checker

explanation.surface: A former auditor looks over someone's money.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exchequer is the British government department that holds public funds.
explanation.definitionFit: The national treasury holds the money of a state.

clue.text: By God! Good man brought in is intellectual

indicators.note: one piece is brought inside another, so it ends up within the exclamation

parts.note: egad is an old oath meaning by God
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise that the good fellow brought in is a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A highbrow, bookish person is a colloquial term for a brainy type.

clue.text: Reported attitude in local copper's area

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the answer sounds like the synonym

parts.note: a manner is a bearing or attitude

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood police officer's district is said to reflect a certain attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; a copper is British slang for a police officer, whose patch is called their manor.
explanation.definitionFit: In British police slang this word means the district an officer patrols.

clue.text: Note essential to Purcell?

parts.note: the central letter of the composer's surname is C, and a musical note named by its central position fits the description

explanation.definitionFit: This is the musical note in the centre of the piano keyboard.

clue.text: Agreed to return convict to part of Ireland

parts.note: done means agreed, as in it's a deal

indicators.note: to return here means to go back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a lag is a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: Officials have agreed to send a prisoner back to an Irish county.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a county in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Place where vulgar swearword is heard

indicators.note: is heard means the words are spoken, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: low means coarse or vulgar; a cuss is a curse or swearword

explanation.surface: Somewhere a coarse oath can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for a site is used in English for a position or location.

clue.text: Treatment for the injured in dirty rugby match?

definitions.meaning: a soak in warm mineral mud is a spa therapy for aches and injuries
a game played on a sodden pitch leaves the players caked in muck

explanation.surface: Players hurt in a filthy rugby game need therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa soak in mud is a therapy; a game on a sodden pitch turns into a muddy wallow.

clue.text: A short cut military leader's taken to produce weapon

indicators.note: the haircut has taken in a letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a bob is a short haircut

indicators.note: a leader is a first letter, so this picks the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A soldier's commander opts for a brief trim before making a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to produce' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomic bomb is a nuclear weapon.

clue.text: A pet appearing to grow less

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, and bate is a British word for a fit of temper

explanation.surface: A pet animal seems to be shrinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing to' is a link; 'pet' is the sulk, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish or subside is to lessen in strength.

clue.text: Restored balance, for the most part, to a wobbly craft?

indicators.note: restored means put back together in a new arrangement
most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Balance is put right on a rocking boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' gives BALANC; with TOA these rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow barge used on inland waterways is a kind of craft.

clue.text: Be trying to hear directions

indicators.note: to hear means spoken aloud, so the answer sounds like the synonym

parts.note: tacks are the directions a sailing boat takes against the wind

explanation.surface: Someone is struggling to make out the instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain someone's patience is to make demands on them.

clue.text: Still a legend, I won't be seen

indicators.note: something not seen is missing, so the letter is removed

parts.note: the yeti is a legendary creature of the Himalayas

explanation.surface: A creature of legend remains elusive, says an observer.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means even so or up to now, both senses of still.

clue.text: Expedition shown by TV finding valuable container

parts.note: dispatch means speed or expedition in getting things done
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: A television expedition uncovers a treasure chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' means promptness, not a journey; 'shown by' and 'finding' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A case for official papers, as at the British Parliament's dispatch box, holds important documents.
